is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae, An. coluzzii, and An. arabiensis (Abstract, Page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper models the frequency of Vgsc-995S and Vgsc-995F (Abstract, Page 3).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper presents model predictions and maps rather than extractable primary genotype counts or frequencies for specific field populations. It uses a database of 2418 observations from other sources (Page 3, Page 16).

african_field_population.evidence: The data used in the model comes from field sampled mosquitoes collected from 27 countries in Africa (Page 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a spatiotemporal modelling paper that re-analyses previously published and aggregated database data (Moyes et al. 2019b) rather than reporting new primary empirical genotype data (Abstract, Page 16).

sub_country_location.evidence: The database used includes geographic coordinates of the sample collection locations (Page 16).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study covers the period 2005-2017 (Abstract, Page 3).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The paper explicitly states: 'Our models are informed by a database... an updated version of a publicly available data set containing Vgsc allele frequencies (Moyes et al. 2019b)' (Page 16).

supplement.evidence: The primary genotype data is not reported in the paper or its supplements, but is sourced from an external database (Moyes et al. 2019b).

assessment.summary: This study is a spatiotemporal modelling paper that uses a large database of previously published and unpublished Vgsc genotype frequencies (primarily from Moyes et al. 2019b) to predict trends across Africa. It does not report new primary genotype data.
exclusion_reasons: is_primary_study: This is a spatiotemporal modelling paper that re-analyses previously published and aggregated database data (Moyes et al. 2019b) rather than reporting new primary empirical genotype data.
reports_extractable_genotype_data: The paper presents model predictions and maps rather than extractable primary genotype counts or frequencies for specific field populations.
